0.why: MicroVOctMapper.cpp:164-177 sets the channel count from getChannels, reads getPolyVoltageSimd and takes a ceiling and a floor of the voltage, so it lands on whole keys
MicroVOctMapper.cpp:185-197 writes one voltage per channel with setVoltageSimd and sets the channel count from the input; the voltage is the base-two logarithm of the frequency ratio

comment: The module turns the input voltage into a pair of whole numbers, a count of the tuning's two generating intervals, then gives each interval the size the chosen tuning gives it (MicroVOctMapper.cpp:29-40 and 167-190). In the two Cleantone tunings the octave is not a two to one ratio, so a scale octave is not 1V: the 5-limit setting builds the octave from a 5/4 and a 3/2, which comes to about 2.01 rather than 2. The black key mapping is part of the arithmetic, shifting the boundary between sharps and flats (the r term at line 173). Two parameters are declared, Sub Freq and Sub3 Freq, and the widget adds no control for either, so neither can be clicked and neither gets a line; nothing in process reads them. The panel's keyboard drawing and tuning name are plain widgets.
